title: FTC administrative reports show higher reported fraud losses in 2025, led by investment and imposter categories
source_unit: FTC consumer fraud reports summarized in congressional testimony
geography: United States consumer reports received by the FTC

imposter_reported_losses.unit: US dollars reported lost, more than

investment_scam_reported_losses.unit: US dollars reported lost, more than

observations.method: FTC administrative totals reported in testimony before the Joint Economic Committee; approximate and lower-bound language is preserved.
observations.uncertainty: Reports are unverified, may include multiple contributors and reporting changes, and undercount fraud that is not reported. Dollar totals are reported losses, not a complete loss census or verified recovery measure.
observations.subgroup: All consumer fraud reports, with imposter and investment-scam categories retained separately.
observations.counterinterpretation: A rise in reported losses can reflect reporting propensity, high-value cases, category or coverage changes, and not only more fraud or greater population exposure.

observations.method: FTC testimony comparison of the 2025 imposter-scam report and loss frame with 2020, retaining approximate language.
observations.uncertainty: The comparison is bounded by FTC administrative reporting and does not establish a comparable population denominator, incidence rate, or causal effect of a particular platform, payment rail, or scam tactic.
observations.subgroup: Imposter scams within the FTC fraud-report taxonomy.
observations.counterinterpretation: Category salience and reporting access may rise over time even if underlying exposure changes differently; the aggregate does not reveal who recovered money or bore the final loss.

related_sources.claim: The Federal Reserve SHED supplies a separate household exposure, loss, recovery, and time-cost frame.
related_sources.access_boundary: The survey and FTC administrative reports have different units, coverage, definitions, and underreporting properties; they must not be pooled.

boundary: This record establishes a later FTC administrative report and reported-loss frame. It does not establish population prevalence, verified harm, recovery, remedy adequacy, trust change, or the same-person household path.
